analysis:
This PR only changes CI plumbing: a new reusable workflow (.github/workflows/darkbloom-route.yml) that picks a runner per lane, wired into ci.yml, desktop.yml, docs-impact.yml and landing.yml. It adds timeouts and moves the component classifier to a GitHub-hosted runner. No provider, coordinator, attestation, key or prefix-cache code (T-041 etc.) changes, so no canonical threat IDs are affected.

Checks on the router:
- Routing is off unless the DARKBLOOM_ROUTING variable is exactly 'on'.
- Fork pull requests fall back to Blacksmith labels without any request to the plane (darkbloom-route.yml lines 88-90). A null or empty head repo also falls back, so it fails closed.
- The plane URL must be https. curl is limited to --proto =https, 5 s, 64 KiB and one retry.
- The plane reply is schema-checked. A plane-chosen runs_on is accepted only if it equals the hardcoded profile label array (line 141). The plane cannot inject arbitrary labels.
- Plane text is sanitised before it is printed (the clean function, lines 53, 130, 144).
- The select job has permissions {} and sends only the repository name, run id and attempt.
- Callers keep contents: read. No secrets are passed to the route job.
- If route fails, the dependent jobs skip and the provider-test-gate (ci.yml 570-592) fails closed.

Residual questions outside the supplied evidence:
- Whether the Darkbloom self-hosted runners are ephemeral and isolated.
- Whether same-repo PR code on those runners could poison actions/cache entries. The workflows use actions/cache restore/save, at ci.yml 234-248 and 608-636.
- How the plane authenticates or authorises route requests.
These are CI-infrastructure concerns, not provider threat-model regressions, so they are noted without a finding. A same-repo PR author can edit the routing workflow, but that already requires write access.
